title: You Didn't Want a Tumble Dryer. So You Built a Tower.
description:
Drying clothes indoors makes the whole house damp, and a tumble dryer costs money every time you run it. So you put up a washing line.

The first part is how a rotary washing line really goes in: dig a hole in the lawn, drop in a ground socket, fill round it with quick-setting concrete and hold it level while it sets. Then the line slots in.

Everything after the rain is a joke. Please do not build a wind tower in your garden.

Washing line sources:
- Lakeland, How to securely put up your rotary airer: https://www.lakeland.co.uk/blogs/inspiration/how-to-securely-put-up-your-new-rotary-airer
- Build-Construct, Installing a rotary washing line: https://build-construct.com/building/installing-a-rotary-washing-line-that-stands-firm-for-years/
- Tarmac Postcrete data sheet (via Wickes): https://media.wickes.co.uk/is/content/wickes/B3182_221100_TECH_0
